issues.label: Applicability of jurisdictional-priority rule
issues.why: Wendee's earlier-filed, first-served Franklin County case may deprive Perry County of authority to proceed.

issues.label: Whether venue and jurisdiction are distinct
issues.why: The court must distinguish improper venue from lack of subject-matter jurisdiction under the priority rule.

issues.label: Proper venue under Civ.R. 3(C)
issues.why: Whether Franklin County qualifies under any subsection of the multiple permissive venue provisions.

issues.label: Exclusivity of Civ.R. 3(C)(9) 90-day rule
issues.why: Whether the divorce-specific residency provision overrides other permissible venue bases in Civ.R. 3(C).

issues.label: 90-day residency computation
issues.why: Whether Wendee met or failed the 90-day Franklin County residency requirement before filing.

issues.label: Effect of improper venue on priority rule
issues.why: Robert argues the priority rule does not apply when the first court lacks proper venue.

issues.label: Proper remedy for improper venue
issues.why: Civ.R. 3 provides for transfer, not dismissal, so dismissal may be erroneous.

issues.label: Whether Civ.R. 12(B)(3) permits dismissal
issues.why: Improper venue ordinarily requires transfer under Civ.R. 3(D) rather than outright dismissal.

issues.label: Distinction between the two complaints' filing dates
issues.why: Wendee filed April 1; Robert filed April 6; ordering priority matters.

issues.label: Service perfection and its priority effect
issues.why: Perfected service in Franklin County first may fix jurisdiction there under the priority rule.

issues.label: Effect of Perry County's prior order
issues.why: Whether the Perry County ruling on venue binds or influences the Franklin County court.

issues.label: Res judicata/collateral estoppel from Perry ruling
issues.why: The prior venue determination may preclude relitigation between the same parties.

issues.label: Effect of Fifth District's mootness dismissal
issues.why: The appellate dismissal of the prohibition writ may affect available remedies and finality.

issues.label: Adequate remedy at law via appeal
issues.why: The Fifth District held appeal was adequate, shaping the procedural posture.

issues.label: Whether both actions involve same claim/parties
issues.why: The priority rule requires the cases be substantially the same for it to apply.

issues.label: Trial court's fairness-based analysis
issues.why: The court's discretionary 'unfairness' standard for applying Civ.R. 3(C)(9) may lack legal basis.

issues.label: Standard of review on motion to dismiss
issues.why: The applicable standard governs how facts and legal conclusions are evaluated.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction over divorce
issues.why: Domestic relations jurisdiction and residency prerequisites must be satisfied independent of venue.

issues.label: Move to Perry County altering venue analysis
issues.why: The June 2024 relocation affects which county satisfies residency and venue rules.
